contentFindings: The quantitative salt and trace-dye assumptions make the predicted initial directions physically coherent; the current target and image depict the intended diffusion/osmosis distinction.

The two mandatory application cases use the identical bag, membrane permeability, salt, dye and task. Their concentrations are merely reversed, so both dye diffusion and osmosis point inward in the first case and outward in the second.

The biology positive-understanding-evidence-v2 criteria require two cases with substantive variation, explicitly ruling out a mere numerical change. The declared permeability variation axis is not exercised across these two cases. A learner could answer both directions by one shared arrow without separately resolving opposing gradients.
repairSuggestion: Keep the first case. In the second, make the dye gradient oppose the impermeant-salt gradient, while specifying the same trace contribution and equal initial pressure: for example, 20 mmol/L impermeant salt inside and 100 mmol/L outside, but dye 0.001 mmol/L inside and 0.01 mmol/L outside. Then dye diffuses inward while water moves outward; require separate membrane/gradient explanations in German and English. Recheck the new case and current bindings before registration.
